name: Zosteropidae
description: White-eyes are a large family of small passerine birds found across Africa, Asia, and Australasia. They are named for the distinctive white eye-ring that most species possess and are highly active, social birds.

children.name: Tephrozosterops
children.description: Tephrozosterops — a genus of white-eyes in the family Zosteropidae.

children.name: Tephrozosterops stalkeri
children.description: The rufescent darkeye (Tephrozosterops stalkeri), also known as the bicoloured white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is monotypic within the genus Tephrozosterops. It is endemic to the island of Seram in Indonesia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Zosterops
children.description: The largest genus of white-eyes, with over 100 species found across the Old World tropics.

children.name: Zosterops albogularis
children.description: The white-chested white-eye (Zosterops albogularis) also known as white-breasted white-eye or Norfolk white-eye was a passerine from the family Zosteropidae. It was endemic to Norfolk Island between New Caledonia and New Zealand and was regarded as either extremely rare or possibly extinct. Since 2000 the Australian government has considered the species extinct.

children.name: Zosterops aldabrensis
children.description:
The Aldabra white-eye (Zosterops aldabrensis) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the island of Aldabra in the Indian Ocean.
The Aldabra white-eye was formerly treated as a subspecies of the Malagasy white-eye (Zosterops maderaspatanus) but based on the results of a molecular phylogenetic study published in 2014, it is now treated as a separate species.

children.name: Zosterops anomalus
children.description: The black-ringed white-eye or lemon-throated white-eye (Zosterops anomalus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops atriceps
children.description:
The cream-throated white-eye (Zosterops atriceps) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the northern Moluccas.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest. They can be found on the Maluku Utara in Indonesia.

children.name: Zosterops atrifrons
children.description:
The black-crowned white-eye (Zosterops atrifrons) is a songbird species. It is closely related to the Old World babblers, and its family Zosteropidae might better be included in the Tiimalidae. Its subspecies from the Sulawesi region might warrant recognition as distinct species Z. Subatrifrons. The Sangihe white-eye (Z. Nehrkorni) and the Seram white-eye (Z. Stalkeri) were formerly included in Z. Atrifrons, as is still, on occasion, the black-fronted white-eye (Z. Minor).
It is endemic to Indonesia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. Quite common, it is not considered a threatened species by the IUCN.

children.name: Zosterops atricapilla
children.description: The black-capped white-eye (Zosterops atricapilla) is a small passerine from the family Zosteropidae.

children.name: Zosterops auriventer
children.description:
Hume's white-eye (Zosterops auriventer) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in upland areas of Myanmar, southern Thailand, the Malay Peninsula and Borneo.
This species was formerly treated as a subspecies of the Indian white-eye (Zosterops palpebrosus). Based on a study published as two articles in 2017, it was promoted to species rank. Included as subspecies are two taxa that were previously treated as subspecies of Everett's white-eye (Zosterops everetti).

children.name: Zosterops borbonicus
children.description: The Réunion grey white-eye (Zosterops borbonicus) is a small passerine from the family Zosteropidae, which is native to the islands of Réunion.

children.name: Zosterops brunneus
children.description:
The Fernando Po speirops (Zosterops brunneus), also known as the Bioko speirops, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Bioko Island in Equatorial Guinea.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland. The species is wholly restricted to the higher elevations of Pico Basilé. It is threatened by habitat loss and is considered vulnerable under the IUCN Red List of threatened species.

children.name: Zosterops buruensis
children.description: The Buru white-eye (Zosterops buruensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Indonesian islands, including the island of Buru which gives its name. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. The species occupy an area of larger than 20,000 km2 and is thought to have a stable population of above 10,000, and thus are not considered as threatened.

children.name: Zosterops ceylonensis
children.description: The Sri Lanka white-eye (Zosterops ceylonensis) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family, which is endemic to Sri Lanka. It is a resident breeder in forests, gardens and plantations, mainly in the highlands.

children.name: Zosterops chloris
children.description:
The lemon-bellied white-eye (Zosterops chloris) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Indonesia, where it occurs on a number of islands from the Sunda Strait to the Aru Islands. It is present on several of the Lesser Sunda Islands as well as on parts of Sulawesi, as well as many smaller islands, but is absent from the larger islands of Borneo, Java, Sumatra and Timor. Currently (May 2017), HBW describes five sub-species of lemon-bellied white-eye. However, the extensive distribution of Z. C. Intermedius (including S. Sulawesi, SE. Sulawesi, C. Lesser Sundas and small islands in between) is likely to contain more than one reproductively isolated population (cf. Z.c. Intermedius and Z. C. Flavissimus, with the latter now considered a distinct species, the Wakatobi white-eye (Z. Flavissimus).
The lemon-bellied white-eye's natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests. On the islands of Buton and Kabaena the lemon-bellied white-eye appears limited to coastal regions, perhaps as a result of competition with the pale-bellied white-eye. Observations from Buton suggest that the lemon-bellied white-eye prefers more disturbed habitats. Their diet consists of invertebrates, fruits, and nectar. They have strong dark grey legs, a dark colored beak, and generally range in size from 11 to 12 cm. They are a yellow-olive color on the dorsal side, with characteristic bright yellow underparts.

children.name: Zosterops chloronothos
children.description: The Mauritius olive white-eye (Zosterops chloronothos, often mistakenly spelled Zosterops chloronothus) is a very rare and localized passerine from the family of white-eyes (Zosteropidae). It is one of two white-eye species endemic to the island of Mauritius, the other being the Mauritius grey white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops chrysolaemus
children.description:
The black-fronted white-eye (Zosterops chrysolaemus) is a songbird species. It is closely related to the Old World babblers, and its family Zosteropidae might better be included in the Tiimalidae. The black-fronted white-eye was formerly considered a subspecies of the green-fronted white-eye (Zosterops minor), and until it was split as a distinct species, the name "black-fronted white-eye" was also used for Z. Minor.
It is found in New Guinea. Quite common, it is considered of least concern by the IUCN.

children.name: Zosterops cinereus
children.description:
The Kosrae white-eye (Zosterops cinereus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Kosrae Island. This species and the grey-brown white-eye were formerly considered conspecific.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Zosterops citrinella
children.description:
The ashy-bellied white-eye (Zosterops citrinella) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae found in the Lesser Sunda Islands in the Indonesian Archipelago and northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, Australia. It is sometimes called the pale white-eye or pale-bellied white-eye, but should not be confused with the pale-bellied white-eye (Zosterops consobrinorum).
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.

children.name: Zosterops consobrinorum
children.description: The pale-bellied white-eye (Zosterops consobrinorum) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to SE Sulawesi in Indonesia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest. The species has a limited distribution and also appears to be sensitive to human disturbance.

children.name: Zosterops conspicillatus
children.description: The bridled white-eye (Zosterops conspicillatus) (Chamorro name: nosa) is a species of white-eye native to the Mariana Islands and formerly Guam. The species' natural habitat is tropical forests, shrublands and urban areas.

children.name: Zosterops dehaani
children.description: The Morotai white-eye (Zosterops dehaani) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Morotai in the northern Moluccas. It was separated from the cream-throated white-eye based on distinct plumage, exceptional dawn song, and submontane/montane ecology

children.name: Zosterops erythropleurus
children.description: The chestnut-flanked white-eye (Zosterops erythropleurus) is a bird in the family Zosteropidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1863. It is found in forests, and prefers rather deep mixed and coniferous forests.

children.name: Zosterops eurycricotus
children.description:
The broad-ringed white-eye (Zosterops eurycricotus) or Kilimanjaro white-eye is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in northeast Tanzania.
The broad-ringed white-eye was formerly considered a subspecies of the montane white-eye, now Heuglin's white-eye (Zosterops poliogastrus).

children.name: Zosterops everetti
children.description: Everett's white-eye (Zosterops everetti) is a bird species in the disputed family Zosteropidae, which might belong with the Old World babblers (Timaliidae). The name commemorates British colonial administrator and zoological collector Alfred Hart Everett. It is only found on the Talaud Islands, Sulu Archipelago and the Philippines. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forests and tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops explorator
children.description:
The Fiji white-eye (Zosterops explorator) is a species of passerine bird in the white-eye family Zosteropidae. The species is also known as Layard's white-eye.
It is endemic to the islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Taveuni, Kadavu, and Ovalau in Fiji, where it is a common bird of forests. Where it co-occurs with the closely related silvereye it is more common in denser forest.

children.name: Zosterops feae
children.description: The São Tomé white-eye (Zosterops feae) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the island of São Tomé, where it occurs in the central massif and in the southwest. Its natural habitat is mid- to high-altitude forests. It is threatened by habitat loss. It was named by the Italian Tommaso Salvadori in 1901.

children.name: Zosterops ficedulinus
children.description: The Príncipe white-eye (Zosterops ficedulinus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. The species was described by Gustav Hartlaub in 1866. It is endemic to the islands of Príncipe and São Tomé, where it is restricted to the hilly interiors of the southern parts. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops finschii
children.description:
The dusky white-eye (Zosterops finschii) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Palau.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops flavifrons
children.description: The Vanuatu white-eye or yellow-fronted white-eye (Zosterops flavifrons) is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Zosterops in the white-eye family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Vanuatu, where it is one of the most common birds.

children.name: Zosterops flavissimus
children.description: The Wakatobi white-eye (Zosterops flavissimus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Indonesia, where it is known only from the Wakatobi Islands off south-eastern Sulawesi. It can be distinguished from most other Indonesian white-eyes by its bright yellow belly. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the lemon-bellied white-eye (Z. Chloris), but it was long known to be reproductively isolated from the rest of the species, and a 2019 genetic study found it to be a distinct species.

children.name: Zosterops fuscicapilla
children.description: The capped white-eye (Zosterops fuscicapilla) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in New Guinea. Its natural habitat is in subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. It has a white eye ring, round wings, and strong legs. The capped white-eyes are sociable and live in large flocks. The Oya Tabu white-eye of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands has sometimes been considered to be a distinct species.

children.name: Zosterops goodfellowi
children.description: Endemic to montane forests of Mindanao in the Philippines, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a bold white eye-ring. It forages actively in the forest canopy.

children.name: Zosterops grandis
children.description: Endemic to the island of New Guinea, this is one of the largest white-eye species with olive-green upperparts, pale yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops grayi
children.description:
The Kai Besar white-eye (Zosterops grayi), also known as the pearl-bellied white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is native to the Kai Islands in Indonesia.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops griseotinctus
children.description:
The Louisiade white-eye or islet white-eye (Zosterops griseotinctus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Papua New Guinea, where it is found on widely disjunct islets on both the Bismarck and Louisiade archipelagos.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops griseovirescens
children.description:
The Annobón white-eye (Zosterops griseovirescens) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the island of Annobón, part of Equatorial Guinea. It was listed as vulnerable by the IUCN until 2021 when they updated its status to least concern.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and plantations.

children.name: Zosterops halmaheranus
children.description: Endemic to Halmahera in the Moluccas of Indonesia, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, yellow underparts, and a bold white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland and montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops hamlini
children.description: The Bougainville white-eye (Zosterops hamlini) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found on Bougainville Island. Its natural habitat is in subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. The Bougainville white-eye was formerly considered a subspecies of the grey-throated white-eye (Zosterops fuscicapilla).

children.name: Zosterops inornatus
children.description: The large Lifou white-eye (Zosterops inornatus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to New Caledonia.

children.name: Zosterops japonicus
children.description: The warbling white-eye (Zosterops japonicus) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family. The specific epithet is occasionally written japonica, but this is incorrect due to the gender of the genus. Its native range includes much of East Asia, including the Russian Far East, Japan, Indonesia, Korea, and the Philippines. It has been intentionally introduced to other parts of the world as a pet and as pest control, with mixed results. As one of the native species of the Japanese islands, it has been depicted in Japanese art on numerous occasions, and historically was kept as a cage bird.

children.name: Zosterops kaffensis
children.description: The Kafa white-eye (Zosterops kaffensis) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family, Zosteropidae. It is found in west and southwest Ethiopia as well as on Mount Kulal in north Kenya. It was formerly considered to be a subspecies of Ethiopian white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops kikuyuensis
children.description: The Kikuyu white-eye (Zosterops kikuyuensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of montane white-eye (Z. Poliogastrus). It is found in central Kenya, in the Aberdare Mountains and on Mount Kenya. IUCN categorizes it as of least concern.

children.name: Zosterops kirki
children.description: Kirk's white-eye (Zosterops kirki) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the Comoros Islands. It was previously considered a subspecies of the Malagasy white-eye. Its common and binomial name are in honour of explorer John Kirk.

children.name: Zosterops kulalensis
children.description: The Ethiopian white-eye (Zosterops poliogastrus), formerly known as Heuglin's white-eye or montane white-eye, is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family Zosteropidae. It is found in southeast Sudan, Eritrea and north, central and east Ethiopia. Its natural habitats range from subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, to subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, plantations, and rural gardens.

children.name: Zosterops lacertosus
children.description:
Sanford's white-eye (Zosterops lacertosus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Nendo Island. It is named after Leonard Cutler Sanford, a trustee of the American Museum of Natural History.
Z. Lacertosus is monotypic (there are no subspecies).

children.name: Zosterops lateralis
children.description:
The silvereye or wax-eye (Zosterops lateralis), also known by its Māori name tauhou, is a very small omnivorous passerine bird of the south-west Pacific. In Australia and New Zealand its common name is sometimes white-eye, but this name is more commonly used to refer to all members of the genus Zosterops, or the entire family Zosteropidae.
In New Zealand, the silvereye was first recorded in 1832. It arrived in greater numbers in 1856, and it is assumed that a migrating flock was swept eastwards by a storm. As an apparently self-introduced bird it is protected as a native New Zealand species. Its Māori name, tauhou, means "stranger" or more literally, "new arrival".

children.name: Zosterops luteus
children.description: The canary white-eye or yellow white-eye (Zosterops luteus) is a species of white-eye endemic to northern Australia in subtropical or tropical mangrove forests. Its common name reflects the circle of white feathers around its eye.

children.name: Zosterops luteirostris
children.description: The Gizo white-eye or yellow-billed white-eye (Zosterops luteirostris) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae.

children.name: Zosterops maderaspatanus
children.description: The Malagasy white-eye (Zosterops maderaspatanus) is a species of bird in the white-eye family, Zosteropidae. Found in Madagascar and Seychelles, its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical mangrove forests, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops mayottensis
children.description:
The Mayotte white-eye or chestnut-sided white-eye (Zosterops mayottensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is now found only on Mayotte in the Comoro Islands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
The Marianne white-eye formerly considered as subspecies of Mayotte white-eye occurred on Marianne and perhaps other islands in the Seychelles but is now extinct.

children.name: Zosterops mbuluensis
children.description:
The Mbulu white-eye (Zosterops mbuluensis) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in southern Kenya and northern Tanzania.
The Mbulu white-eye was formerly treated as a subspecies of the montane white-eye (Zosterops poliogastrus). When a molecular phylogenetic study published in 2014 found that it was more closely related to the Abyssinian white-eye (Zosterops abyssinicus), the Mbulu white-eye was promoted to species rank. It is monotypic.

children.name: Zosterops meeki
children.description: The Tagula white-eye or white-throated white-eye (Zosterops meeki) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Zosterops meratusensis
children.description:
The Meratus white-eye (Zosterops meratusensis) is a species of bird in the white-eye family, Zosteropidae. The species was described in 2021 by the Indonesian ornithologist Mohammed Irham and his colleagues based on genetic, morphological, and vocal differences from other Zosterops white-eyes. It is endemic to the Meratus Mountains of Indonesian Borneo, where it has been observed on Mount Besar and Mount Karokangen. It inhabits the mid and lower storeys of closed-canopy montane forests at elevations between. It is a typical Zosterops white-eye, with deep olive-green upperparts, yellower underparts, a yellow stripe across the lores, and a distinctive bicoloured bill. Adults have a length of around and a mass. Both sexes look alike.
Most aspects of the Meratus white-eye's ecology are unknown. It has it has been seen in mixed-species foraging flocks with other insectivores. Its breeding is also poorly studied, but presumed juveniles have been seen in the second week of July. The species is classified as being of least-concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) on the IUCN Red List. It is thought to be locally common within the small area it inhabits and is not currently threatened, although the songbird trade may represent a future threat. Recommended conservation measures for the species include surveys to accurately estimate its population, finding the demand for the species in the songbird trade, and finding suitable tracts of habitat to protect.

children.name: Zosterops meyeni
children.description: The lowland white-eye (Zosterops meyeni) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is near endemic to the northern part of the Philippines but is also found on the Taiwanese islands of Lüdao and Lanyu. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forest, second growth and gardens.

children.name: Zosterops minor
children.description:
The green-fronted white-eye (Zosterops minor) is a songbird species. It is closely related to the Old World babblers, and its family Zosteropidae might better be included in the Tiimalidae. Some sources include this species within Z. Atrifrons, the black-crowned white-eye. The black-fronted white-eye (Z. Chrysolaemus) was formerly considered a subspecies, and until it was split as a distinct species, the name "black-fronted white-eye" was also used for Z. Minor.
It is found in New Guinea and offshore islands. Quite common, it is not considered a threatened species by the IUCN.

children.name: Zosterops mizanensis
children.description: Found in the highlands of southwestern Ethiopia, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests and bamboo.

children.name: Zosterops modestus
children.description: The Seychelles white-eye (Zosterops modestus) is a rare warbler-like perching bird from the family of white-eyes (Zosteropidae). It is endemic to the Seychelles. At one time thought to be extinct, it was rediscovered and is now listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN.

children.name: Zosterops montanus
children.description: The warbling white-eye (Zosterops japonicus) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family. The specific epithet is occasionally written japonica, but this is incorrect due to the gender of the genus. Its native range includes much of East Asia, including the Russian Far East, Japan, Indonesia, Korea, and the Philippines. It has been intentionally introduced to other parts of the world as a pet and as pest control, with mixed results. As one of the native species of the Japanese islands, it has been depicted in Japanese art on numerous occasions, and historically was kept as a cage bird.

children.name: Zosterops mouroniensis
children.description:
The Karthala white-eye (Zosterops mouroniensis), also known as the Mount Karthala white-eye, Grand Comore white-eye, or Comoro white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. As suggested by its name, it is endemic to Philippia heath woodland growing on Mount Karthala on the island of Grand Comore in the Comoros. Mount Karthala is an active volcano and future eruptions pose a serious threat to the Karthala white-eye. The bird is further threatened by human-induced habitat loss.
The bird is approximately long with olive upperparts and yellow-green underparts. It has a white ring around the eye. Its diet consists of fruits and insects.

children.name: Zosterops murielae
children.description: Endemic to Vanikoro Island in the Solomon Islands, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops mysorensis
children.description:
The Biak white-eye (Zosterops mysorensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the islands of Biak and Supiori in West Papua, Indonesia.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops natalis
children.description: The Christmas white-eye (Zosterops natalis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Christmas Island. Its natural habitats are tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland. It is threatened by habitat destruction.

children.name: Zosterops nehrkorni
children.description:
The Sangihe white-eye (Zosterops nehrkorni) is a species of bird in the white-eye family. It is endemic to Sangihe, Indonesia.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops nigrorum
children.description: The yellowish white-eye (Zosterops nigrorum) or golden-yellow white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the Philippines. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops novaeguineae
children.description: The Papuan white-eye (Zosterops novaeguineae), sometimes known as the New Guinea white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in the Aru Islands and New Guinea (mainly Huon, Bird's Head and Papuan Peninsula). Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. The species was first classified in 1878, and has a conservation status of Least Concern.

children.name: Zosterops obbiensis
children.description: Found in coastal Somalia, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits dry scrub and coastal vegetation.

children.name: Zosterops olivaceus
children.description: The Réunion olive white-eye (Zosterops olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found on Réunion. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland.

children.name: Zosterops pallidus
children.description: The Orange River white-eye (Zosterops pallidus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae, which is native to Namibia and South Africa. It was formerly deemed conspecific with the Cape white-eye (Zosterops virens), but the two species occur sympatrically in central South Africa, and they are genetically distinct.

children.name: Zosterops poliogastrus
children.description: The Ethiopian white-eye (Zosterops poliogastrus), formerly known as Heuglin's white-eye or montane white-eye, is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family Zosteropidae. It is found in southeast Sudan, Eritrea and north, central and east Ethiopia. Its natural habitats range from subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, to subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, plantations, and rural gardens.

children.name: Zosterops rendovae
children.description:
The Makira white-eye (Zosterops rendovae), also known as the grey-throated white-eye, is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family, Zosteropidae. It is also known as Zosterops ugiensis because Z. Rendovae has often been used for the Solomons white-eye (Z. Kulambangrae).
It is endemic to the island of Makira in the Solomon Islands archipelago. The Guadalcanal white-eye (Z. Oblitus) on Guadalcanal and Bougainville white-eye (Z. Hamlini) on Bougainville were formerly considered subspecies, but are now considered distinct species. It inhabits primary forest, mainly at 900–2000 m above sea-level but small numbers occur at lower levels.

children.name: Zosterops rodericanus
children.description: Endemic to Rodrigues Island in the Mascarene Islands, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It is common in forests and gardens.

children.name: Zosterops rotensis
children.description: The Rota white-eye or Rota bridled white-eye (Zosterops rotensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is critically endangered and endemic to Rota in the Northern Mariana Islands, where it mainly occurs in mature, wet limestone forests.

children.name: Zosterops samoensis
children.description:
The Samoan white-eye (Zosterops samoensis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the island of Savai'i in Samoa.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops santaecrucis
children.description: The Santa Cruz white-eye (Zosterops sanctaecrucis) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the Solomon Islands.

children.name: Zosterops semperi
children.description: The citrine white-eye (Zosterops semperi), or Caroline Islands white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found in Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia.

children.name: Zosterops senegalensis
children.description: The northern yellow white-eye (Zosterops senegalensis), formerly the African yellow white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found across sub-Saharan Africa, from Senegal in the west across to southern Sudan in the east and south to northern Angola. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the Angola white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops silvanus
children.description:
Taita white-eye (Zosterops silvanus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It includes numerous subspecies, sometimes considered a subspecies to montane white-eye (Z. Poliogastrus). It is only found in Taita Hills in southeastern Kenya. IUCN categorizes it as vulnerable. It is threatened by severe habitat loss and fragmentation, mainly as a result of the deforestation of the Taita Hills.
It is often observed in mixed flocks with the pale white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops splendidus
children.description:
The Ranongga white-eye or splendid white-eye (Zosterops splendidus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the Solomon Islands.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops stalkeri
children.description:
The Seram white-eye (Zosterops stalkeri) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family. It is an endemic resident breeder in open woodland in Seram, Indonesia.
It was formerly considered conspecific with black-fronted white-eye, Zosterops minor, but work by Pamela C. Rasmussen and her colleagues showed that it is a separate species. The same research also confirmed the specific status of the Sangihe white-eye, Zosterops nehrkorni.

children.name: Zosterops stierlingi
children.description: Found in the highlands of Tanzania and Malawi, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops strenuus
children.description: The robust white-eye (Zosterops strenuus), also known as the Lord Howe white-eye or robust silvereye and locally as the "big grinnell", is an extinct species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It was endemic to the lowland forests of Lord Howe Island, east of Australia.

children.name: Zosterops taiwanus
children.description: Endemic to Taiwan, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It is common in lowland forests and gardens across the island.

children.name: Zosterops tephropleurus
children.description: The Lord Howe silvereye (Zosterops lateralis tephropleurus), also known as the Lord Howe white-eye, Lord Howe Island white-eye or, locally, as the "Little Grinnell", is a small bird in the white-eye family, Zosteropidae. It is a subspecies of the silvereye (Zosterops lateralis), though sometimes considered a full species. It is endemic to Lord Howe Island in the Tasman Sea, part of New South Wales, Australia.

children.name: Zosterops uropygialis
children.description:
The Kai Kecil white-eye (Zosterops uropygialis), also known as the golden-bellied white-eye, is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is native to the Kai Islands in Indonesia.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops vaughani
children.description:
The Pemba white-eye (Zosterops vaughani) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to Tanzania.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical mangrove forests, and dry savanna.

children.name: Zosterops vellalavella
children.description:
The Vella Lavella white-eye, belted white-eye, or banded white-eye (Zosterops vellalavella) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is endemic to the Solomon Islands.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops virens
children.description: The Cape white-eye (Zosterops virens) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family. It is native to southern Africa. It is commonly found in suburbia, parks and gardens, besides a variety of mesic to well-watered habitats.

children.name: Zosterops winifredae
children.description:
The south Pare white-eye (Zosterops winifredae) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. Its range is restricted to the southern region of the Pare Mountains in northeastern Tanzania.
The south Pare white-eye was formerly treated as a subspecies of the Heuglin's white-eye (Zosterops poliogastrus) (previously named montane white-eye) but it is now considered as a separate species based on the phylogenetic relationships determined in a molecular study published in 2014.

children.name: Zosterops xanthochroa
children.description: The green-backed white-eye (Zosterops xanthochroa) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is also known as the New Caledonian white-eye. It is endemic to New Caledonia.

children.name: Zosterops griseivirens
children.description: Found in the highlands of Tanzania, this white-eye has greyish-olive upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops leucogrammicus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sumatra, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, white underparts with fine dark streaks, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops melanogaster
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sumatra and Java, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts and a distinctive dark grey to black belly. It inhabits montane forests above 1000 metres.

children.name: Zosterops albiventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of Borneo, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pure white underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops stenocricotus
children.description:
The forest white-eye or Cameroon green white-eye (Zosterops stenocricotus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is found from southeastern Nigeria to southwestern Central African Republic and northern Gabon.
Its natural habitats are subtropical, tropical moist montane forests, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Zosterops mauritianus
children.description: The Mauritius grey white-eye (Zosterops mauritianus) is a species of bird in the family Zosteropidae. It is one of two white-eye species endemic to the island of Mauritius, the other being the rare and localized Mauritius olive white-eye. It inhabits woodlands, forests, and gardens. The Réunion grey white-eye is very closely related. They were formerly considered conspecific and together called Mascarene white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops melanurus
children.description:
The sangkar white-eye (Zosterops melanurus) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae. It is also known as the Sunda white-eye. It is found in forested habitats on the Indonesian islands of Java and Bali. In Java it is typically found at elevations between, but it sometimes occurs at lower elevations as well.
This species was formerly treated as conspecific with the Indian white-eye (previously the Oriental white-eye, Zosterops palpebrosus), but based on the results of a molecular phylogenetic study published in 2018, it was promoted to species rank.

children.name: Zosterops flavoviridis
children.description: Found in the Moluccas of Indonesia, this white-eye has bright yellow-green upperparts, yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops limbatus
children.description: Found in the Lesser Sunda Islands, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops platysternus
children.description: Found in the Philippines, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops chlorichroa
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has bright olive-green upperparts, pale green underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops kasaicus
children.description: The Angola white-eye (Zosterops kasaicus), is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family Zosteropidae. It is found from central Democratic Republic of the Congo to northern and central Angola. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the northern yellow white-eye.

children.name: Zosterops pallidiventris
children.description: Found in East Africa, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale whitish underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits coastal forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops capensis
children.description: The Cape white-eye (Zosterops virens) is a small passerine bird in the white-eye family. It is native to southern Africa. It is commonly found in suburbia, parks and gardens, besides a variety of mesic to well-watered habitats.

children.name: Zosterops andamanensis
children.description: Endemic to the Andaman Islands, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It is common in forests across the archipelago.

children.name: Zosterops erythrothorax
children.description: Found in the highlands of Cameroon, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, a distinctive chestnut breast band, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops cameroonensis
children.description: Endemic to Mount Cameroon, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests on the mountain slopes.

children.name: Zosterops orbitalis
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and an exceptionally broad white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops caledonicus
children.description: Endemic to New Caledonia, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits forests and scrub across the island.

children.name: Zosterops luketensis
children.description: Endemic to Socotra Island off the Horn of Africa, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops maculosus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sulawesi, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale underparts with fine dark spotting, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops griseipectus
children.description: Found on the island of Seram in the Moluccas, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops coronatus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sumatra, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, a distinctive yellow crown, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops sulfureus
children.description: Found in the highlands of East Africa, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, bright sulphur-yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops chalybeus
children.description: Found on islands in the Moluccas, this white-eye has grey upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops flavus
children.description:
The Javan white-eye (Zosterops flavus) is a bird species in the family Zosteropidae that occurs in Java and Borneo. It is threatened by trapping for wildlife trade and has been assessed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List in 2019, as the wild population declined significantly.
In West Java, it has been recorded in Pulau Dua, Muara Gembong and Tanjung Sedari between 1984 and 1985. Its natural habitat includes tropical moist lowland and mangrove forests and shrubland.

children.name: Zosterops chloronotus
children.description: The western silvereye (Zosterops lateralis chloronotus) is a small greenish bird in the Zosteropidae or white-eye family.

children.name: Zosterops luteivirens
children.description: Endemic to the Philippines, this white-eye has yellowish-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests and scrub.

children.name: Zosterops aureiventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has golden-yellow underparts, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops brunneiventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of Seram in the Moluccas, this white-eye has brownish underparts, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops flavicollis
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a bright yellow throat, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops griseiviridis
children.description: Found in the highlands of Tanzania, this white-eye has greyish-olive upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops olivaceiventris
children.description: Found in the highlands of eastern Africa, this white-eye has olive-tinged underparts, greyish-olive upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops laticola
children.description: Found in the forests of Central Africa, this white-eye has a broad bill, olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland rainforests.

children.name: Zosterops monticolus
children.description: Found in the highlands of East Africa, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, pale grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops albocingulatus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sumatra, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, white underparts with a distinctive white band across the belly, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops cinereiventris
children.description: Found on islands in the Moluccas, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, ash-grey underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops nigrosternus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sulawesi, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, a distinctive black patch on the breast, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops fusciventris
children.description: Found on islands in the Bismarck Archipelago, this white-eye has olive-green upperparts, dusky brown underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops albifrons
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a white forehead, olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops rufiventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of Seram, this white-eye has rufous-tinged underparts, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops leucops
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a white face, olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops chlorops
children.description: Found in the mountains of Borneo, this white-eye has a greenish face, bright olive upperparts, yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops nigriceps
children.description: Found in the mountains of the Philippines, this white-eye has a black crown and nape, olive-green upperparts, white underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops cinctiventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a distinctive dark band across the belly, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops subcaeruleus
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sulawesi, this white-eye has bluish-tinged upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops chrysops
children.description: Found in the Solomon Islands, this white-eye has a golden-yellow face, olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits lowland forests.

children.name: Zosterops xanthogaster
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has bright yellow underparts, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops griseiceps
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a grey crown, olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops flaviceps
children.description: Found in the mountains of Sulawesi, this white-eye has a yellow crown, olive-green upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops rubriventris
children.description: Found in the mountains of New Guinea, this white-eye has a reddish-buff belly, olive-green upperparts, and a prominent white eye-ring. It inhabits montane forests.

children.name: Zosterops flavifrons alternus
children.description: A subspecies of the Yellow-fronted White-eye found on Tanna Island in Vanuatu, with more extensive yellow on the forehead and brighter underparts.

children.name: Zosterops minor lativirens
children.description: A subspecies of the Black-fronted White-eye found in the mountains of New Guinea, with greener upperparts and a broader black forehead patch.
